ideas.hypothesis: Large one-day drops without company-specific news tend to be liquidity or overreaction moves that partly reverse over the next few days, while drops with news do not.
ideas.rule: BUY at the table's max shares when a name has d1 <= -4.0% and no headline in its theme today names the company; skip if entry cost > 1.3%. Horizon 3 trading days; exit at horizon or the -8% stop.
ideas.source: Lehmann 1990 (QJE) and Jegadeesh 1990 (JF) short-term reversal; Chan 2003 (JFE) 'Stock price reaction to news and no-news'
ideas.note: 0 closed. 2026-11-12: EDV.L d1 -6.03% but two gold_miners headlines name Endeavour (Mana output warning), so it is a news drop and is excluded; its 1.6% entry cost would also fail the 1.3% cap. No trigger.

ideas.hypothesis: Large one-day gains that come with company-specific results or guidance news are under-reacted to and keep drifting for a few days, unlike no-news moves.
ideas.rule: BUY at the table's max shares when a name has d1 >= +4.0% and at least one headline today names the company and reports its results, guidance, forecast or outlook; skip if entry cost > 1.3%. Horizon 3 trading days; exit at horizon or the -8% stop.
ideas.source: Chan 2003 (JFE) news vs no-news; Savor 2012 (JFE) 'Stock returns after major price shocks: the role of information'
